title: Best Incognito Mode Tools Compared - Private Browsing Guide
metaDescription: Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge private modes compared with Tor Browser and Incognito Browser (which we make), each scored on the same rubric.
intro: Not all incognito modes are created equal. Every major browser offers private browsing, but they differ a lot in what they protect. This page compares four built-in private modes with Tor Browser and Incognito Browser on the same four criteria, and each rating is worked out from the table.

products.name: Chrome Incognito Mode
pros: Clear privacy reminder on new tab page
cons: Google can still track browsing
Limited privacy protection
ISP and websites can still see activity

products.name: Firefox Private Browsing
cons: Still allows some fingerprinting
DNS over HTTPS is on by default only in some countries
Some websites may break functionality

products.name: Safari Private Browsing
products.tagline: Safari's private mode on Mac, iPhone and iPad
cons: Only available on Apple devices
Limited customization options
Some advanced features require macOS updates

products.name: Edge InPrivate Browsing
cons: Still sends some data to Microsoft
Less established privacy reputation
Extensions are off in InPrivate unless you allow each one

products.name: Incognito Browser
products.tagline: Android browser that is always in private mode and wipes history, cookies and sessions when you exit
pros: Every tab is private; there is no normal mode to switch out of
History, cookies and sessions are wiped when you exit the app
Keeps no browsing history or cache on the device (downloaded files are kept)
Built-in ad blocker with a High Security Blocking option
cons: Android only: no iOS, desktop or web version
No VPN: sites you visit still see your IP address, and your network and internet provider can see which sites you visit
Does not claim tracker blocking or fingerprinting protection
Google Play's Data safety section says it may collect crash logs and diagnostics

products.name: Tor Browser
products.tagline: Browser that routes your traffic through the Tor network
pros: Isolates cookies to each site and makes users look alike to resist fingerprinting
Hides your IP address from the sites you visit
cons: Slower than a regular browser, because traffic passes through three relays
Some websites block Tor traffic
Many sites show CAPTCHAs to Tor users
May draw unwanted attention

features.name: Tracking Protection
features.description: Blocks advertisers and websites from following your browsing activity across different sites

chrome-incognito.note: Blocks third-party cookies by default; no tracker blocking beyond that

incognito-browser.note: Wipes cookies and sessions when you exit, and cookies can be turned off; the ad blocker blocks ads. Tracker blocking is not claimed

tor-browser.note: Isolates cookies to each site and clears them when you close it

features.name: Fingerprinting Protection
features.description: Prevents websites from identifying you based on browser characteristics and device settings

firefox-private.note: Mozilla's added fingerprinting protections are on by default in private windows

safari-private.note: Advanced Tracking and Fingerprinting Protection is on by default in Private Browsing

incognito-browser.note: Not claimed. Agent Cloaking changes the browser and device a site sees, which is not fingerprint protection

tor-browser.note: Makes every user look alike to resist fingerprinting

features.name: Ease of Use
features.description: How simple it is for average users to access and use the private browsing mode

incognito-browser.note: Always in private mode; no special window to open

features.name: Extension Support
features.description: Ability to use browser extensions while in private browsing mode

safari-private.note: Extensions need permission to run in Private Browsing

edge-inprivate.note: Extensions must be allowed in InPrivate one by one

incognito-browser.note: Extensions are not among its listed features

verdict.summary: On these four criteria Safari Private Browsing scores highest: it blocks known trackers and adds fingerprinting protection by default, but it runs only on Apple devices. Firefox Private Browsing and Tor Browser tie for second (Firefox is listed first alphabetically). Firefox's private windows block known trackers and add fingerprinting protections by default, and Firefox runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. Tor Browser ties Safari for tracking protection, has the strongest fingerprinting protection here and hides your IP address, but it discourages extensions. Edge InPrivate comes next, with three tracking-prevention levels. Chrome Incognito blocks third-party cookies but does little else to stop tracking. Incognito Browser, which we make, scores lowest here: it is always in private mode and wipes history, cookies and sessions when you exit, but it doesn't claim tracker blocking or fingerprinting protection, has no extensions and runs only on Android.

pro_tips: Combine incognito mode with a VPN for better IP address protection - your ISP and network admin can still see your activity otherwise.
Clear your DNS cache after private browsing sessions, as DNS queries may be stored even when using incognito mode.
Remember that incognito mode doesn't hide your activity from your employer, school, or ISP - only from other users of your device.
Close every private window when you finish a sensitive session: most browsers clear private browsing data only once the last private window is closed.
Disable location services and camera/microphone permissions in your browser settings for additional privacy protection during private browsing.

faqs.question: Does incognito mode make me completely anonymous online?
faqs.answer: No, incognito mode only prevents your browser from storing history, cookies, and form data locally. Your ISP, employer, school network, and the websites you visit can still see and track your activity.

faqs.question: Which browser has the best incognito mode for privacy?
faqs.answer: On this page's four criteria Safari Private Browsing scores highest, but it runs only on Apple devices. Firefox Private Browsing and Tor Browser tie for second. Tor Browser ties Safari for tracking protection, has the strongest fingerprinting protection here and hides your IP address, but it is a separate download and discourages extensions.

faqs.question: Can websites detect when I'm using incognito mode?
faqs.answer: Yes, many websites can detect private browsing mode through various techniques. Some sites may restrict content or ask you to disable private browsing. This detection doesn't compromise your privacy but may affect functionality.

faqs.question: Should I use incognito mode for online banking?
faqs.answer: Incognito mode can add a layer of security for banking by not storing login data locally, but it's not necessary for security. Focus on using strong passwords, two-factor authentication, and secure networks instead.

faqs.question: What's the difference between incognito mode and using a VPN?
faqs.answer: Incognito mode only affects local storage on your device, while a VPN encrypts your internet traffic and hides your IP address from websites and your ISP. For better privacy, use both together.
